sections.text_helper: Section 25.4.4 "CCB coupling and chaining" in chapter 25 (Coupling and chaining bridge (CCB)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 749.
sections.section_content:
Note: The selection of these chaining modes is defined in Section25.5. In most of these
operations, a read of the PKA RAM returns 0 (shown with a purple circle in the following
figures).
Coupling CPU → PKA + SAES (write)
When the corresponding OPSTEP is selected, the CCB takes the write requests that go to
the PKA RAM, and sends them to SAES_DINR, as shown in Figure166. Write to
SAES_DINR is not coupled to the PKA. The CCB sends both data and address to
SAES_DINR.
[Figure 166. CCB operation CPU → PKA + SAES (write)]

Chaining PKA → SAES
When the corresponding OPSTEP is selected, for each 32-bit write request tothe PKA RAM
of magic number 0xCCB, the CCB generates a read request from the write target (in the
PKA RAM) to SAES_DINR.

Chaining
Chaining SAES → PKA
When the corresponding OPSTEP is selected, the CCB takes the write requests that go to
the PKA RAM, and substitutes these data by a 32-bit word coming from SAES_DOUTR.
When available, this chaining is activated when the application writes 0xCCB to PKA RAM.
[Figure 168. CCB operation SAES → PKA]
Chaining SAES → CCB
When the corresponding OPSTEP is selected, the CCB takes the read requests to
SAES_DOUTR, and sends them to the system interconnect and to CCB_REFTAGRx
holding the reference TAG information. For confidentiality reason, read data toward system
bus are zeroed by the CCB.
If the CCB finds that the transfered value matches its reference information, it signals to the
PKA that it can proceed with the protected PKA operation (START bit can be set).
[Figure 169. CCB operation SAES → CCB]
Chaining RNG → PKA (write)
When the corresponding OPSTEP is selected, the CCB takes the write requests that go to
the PKA RAM, and substitutes these data with random numbers coming from RNG_DR. For
consistency, the application can write 0xCCB to activate this chaining.
[Figure 170. CCB operation RNG → PKA (write)]
Chaining RNG → SAES (write)
When the corresponding OPSTEP is selected, the CCB takes the write requests that go to
SAES_IVR1 to IVR3, and substitutes these data with random numbers coming from
RNG_DR. For consistency, the application can write 0xCCB to activate this chaining.
[Figure 171. CCB operation RNG → SAES (write)]
